packs.title: Care that carries forward.
packs.lead: MediChain connects the patient experience with the daily work of the care team.
sections: Best Health Solution | FNB App of the Year 2026

A patient should not have to restart their medical story at every handover. MediChain brings patient records, consent, clinical work, diagnostics, medicines and emergency information into connected patient and staff experiences.
One record. Several roles. A visible trail.

The application includes distinct experiences for patients, doctors, nurses, laboratory staff, pharmacists, responders and administrators. Its strongest story is the movement of useful information between those roles.

An implemented application and selected synthetic workflows, supported by source and dated local verification. This is a positioning workshop document, not the final submission. The hosted build and final proof assets will shape the next revision.
Turn fragmented care tasks into a coherent journey that patients can understand and care teams can continue. The following pages show the product value at each step.

packs.title: From one encounter to the next
packs.lead: Six connected moments make the application memorable.
sections: Find the patient and inspect the record, history and observations. The next professional starts with context rather than an empty form.
Capture triage, clinical notes and nursing assessments in structured workflows. Preserve the encounter story for colleagues.
Bring reviewed lab evidence into the chart; connect prescribing and dispensing to the treatment journey.
Use care plans, fluid balance, wounds and SBAR handover to communicate what happened and what needs attention.
Patients can view records, manage access, see recorded disclosures, message the care team and organise appointments and medicines.
Medical identity and scoped emergency access can surface essential information for responders, with a recorded disclosure visible to the patient.

packs.title: A patient experience with agency
packs.lead: The patient portal makes information and access visible.
sections: Records, medical history, observations and laboratory views give the patient a place to inspect their own care context. The value is continuity between encounters.
Consent controls provide a direct way to manage permission. Access history makes recorded use and emergency disclosure inspectable. This is a tangible product benefit that judges can explore.

Appointments, messages, medication views, reminders and symptom tracking provide practical follow-up tools. Their intended benefit is better preparation and less fragmented communication; outcome improvements remain to be measured.
Medical ID and emergency-card workflows organise essential context. A QR download and an explicitly labelled preview are present; the app does not automatically set a phone lock screen.
Family, immunisation and preventive-care capabilities offer longer-term context. Family authorisation needs dedicated qualification before live use.

The 27 September local synthetic run recorded patient/doctor observations read-back, access-history visibility, two-way messages and an authenticated QR download. These are dated demonstration results, not adoption metrics. [E1]

packs.title: A workspace for the care team
packs.lead: A shared patient context supports different professional tasks.
sections: Patient search, chart documents, triage, SOAP/progress notes, history and physical, consultations, discharge, orders and care plans organise the encounter from assessment to follow-up.

Nursing care plans, fluid balance, wound assessments, medication administration and SBAR handover support the details that carry a shift. A 4 October local run proved several durable writes and the incoming nurse handover, while exposing unresolved flowsheet, IV and Morse read-back checks. [E2]
Specimen, results, review and critical-value entry points connect diagnostic work to the chart. Prescription processing and dispensing history give pharmacy its own task-focused path.

Emergency identity, authorised device selection and ambulance handover carry the same patient association into urgent care. Browser demonstration is evidence of a workflow, not certification of physical NFC deployment.

Imaging, pathology, specialist emergencies, procedures and perioperative documentation broaden the product. Administration, identity review, incidents and retention offer governance controls. The evidence appendix lists the qualification task for every family.

packs.title: Trust is part of the experience
packs.lead: The value is visible control, supported by explicit boundaries.
sections: Recorded access reasons and emergency disclosures give the patient a way to understand how information was used. This can make trust discussable in the interface rather than buried in a policy.
Credential sessions, roles, access grants and managed-device workflows provide controls around sensitive tasks. A source-level control is not a completed independent security assessment.
Protected records and signed audit checkpoints
The backend includes encrypted document storage in PostgreSQL and a signed audit stream. External immutable checkpoint copies and deployment hardening still require hosting work. [E3]

Scores, alerts and structured pathways should show their inputs and preserve missing observations as missing. We present these as decision-support capabilities; we do not claim autonomous diagnosis or predictive machine learning.

Judging uses synthetic people and records. Live patient operation requires separate clinical, privacy, security and operational readiness work. The product proposition is continuity with accountability, with progress supported by evidence.

packs.title: A focused commercial proposition
packs.lead: Research how the connected care journey can become a sustainable offering.
sections: A clinic or care organisation coordinating patient follow-up, diagnostic results and staff handovers is a plausible buyer segment to investigate. This is positioning research, not a statement about existing customers.

The commercial proposition combines a patient portal and role-specific workflows, reducing the need to assemble disconnected tools for the same encounter. Time saved and avoided duplication are testable value hypotheses.

Evaluate a facility subscription with transparent onboarding and support. Price by measured operating cost, procurement requirements and willingness to pay. Keep any proposed price separate from an agreed commercial offer.

The hosting plan keeps both frontends, API and database on one AWS server for the synthetic awards workload, with separate backups. Capacity and service eligibility must be measured and checked; credits are temporary. See the existing AWS research brief. [E4]

Should the initial offering focus on records/access, diagnostics-to-treatment and nurse handover? A smaller, clearly qualified bundle may be easier to explain and operate than selling every specialist workflow at once.
Compare buyer needs, support requirements and operating cost before choosing the commercial package. Durable workflow proof and clinical review should guide the offering.

packs.title: Why MediChain deserves a closer look
packs.lead: Judge the connected experience, then examine the evidence.
sections: The differentiating proposition is the combination of patient agency, clinical work, supporting roles and emergency continuity around one patient context. Demonstrate the transitions rather than asking judges to count screens.

The product is designed around continuity, trust and practical access. Low-data performance, full language coverage, offline behaviour and rural field usability are validation priorities, not completed achievements.

Vula Medical reports winning both the overall and health awards in 2025 through its specialist-access/referral proposition. MediChain should show its broader patient-to-care-team continuity clearly, without claiming to outperform an established winner or to be first in the market. [S11]
Patient record and access history; reviewed laboratory evidence in the chart; pharmacy history; nursing handover; scoped emergency context. The judge guide gives a short exploration route.

Review the Capability Evidence appendix alongside this submission. Hosted access details and current demo evidence must be added before entry. The application is ready to tell a product story; the submitted build must substantiate it.

E4: docs/AWS_HOSTING_AND_FNB_AWARDS_RESEARCH_2026-10-07.md. Source repository: github.com/mrlucas679/medichain. S11 is linked in the research brief.

packs.title: Capability and evidence
packs.lead: A complete value map, with qualification separated from source presence.
sections: Each family states the user benefit, the source areas inspected and a concrete demonstration. Source-present means implementation files exist; it does not establish that every route, permission, integration or save/reload journey works.

E1 is the 27 September local synthetic browser verification. E2 is the 4 October nurse journey output: 37 of 41 total steps passed, including 10 session checks and 27 nurse checks; four nurse steps failed. Neither result certifies the current hosted build.

The accompanying CSV enumerates every non-test page component under both portals, plus declared route entries with source lines. Pages without an App.tsx reference are flagged for follow-up rather than silently counted as connected capabilities.

No clinical safety outcome, time saving, partnership, predictive AI accuracy or compliance certification is asserted without independent evidence. This workshop edition excludes user and pilot content at the developer request.
Reviewed on 7 October 2026. No application code changed or services started for this document build. Current deployment and role workflow qualification remain release tasks.

packs.title: Release qualification and claims
packs.lead: Make every major promise inspectable.
sections: Re-run nursing flowsheet, IV/VIP and Morse checks against the chosen judge build. Determine whether each failure is product behaviour, fixture/permission setup or the journey assertion. Resolve or disclose it; do not advertise these as passed.

Use distinct patient and staff browser profiles. Record permission grants/denials, writes, role-to-role read-back, refresh and restart. Keep a build identifier and a dated result ledger. A healthy endpoint is insufficient.

Jitsi: two-device real call. Email/SMS: authenticated delivery and opt-out behaviour. NFC: physical device. Wearables: real provider data. Translation/offline: actual supported coverage and reconnect. Insurance/research: real downstream acceptance if claimed.

Review score formulas, missing-data handling and alert behaviour with qualified clinical reviewers. Report limitations and intended use. Clinical effectiveness has not been measured by these documents.
Attach proof that a judge can follow

Use six current synthetic screenshots with captions: patient record, access history, lab chart evidence, pharmacy history, nurse handover and emergency disclosure. The dated September images are not substituted for a current-build capture.

All capability families derive from current portal page inventory and App.tsx routes. E1/E2 are local records, not independent clinical trials. Backend boundaries derive from CLAUDE.md and relevant API modules. Editable CSVs retain exact relative files and line numbers.

packs.title: Explore the connected care journey
packs.lead: A short guide for hands-on judging | Access edition awaiting hosted details
sections: See what information the patient can view and how access is explained. Then switch to a professional role to see how that context supports a task.

This is the proposed structure for a later judge guide. After AWS hosting, add the verified URL, privately issued synthetic accounts, support contact and exact build through the final submission workflow.
Patient, clinician, nurse, pharmacy, lab and responder accounts should use separate profiles or devices to avoid overwriting a shared session. Start each account at its own assigned portal.
Use the assigned synthetic patient. Older local reports use Naledi Mokoena (Demo), PAT-DEMO-090; the hosted fixture may differ. Do not enter real patient data or call real emergency services.
The same patient context should follow the record, diagnostic evidence, treatment, handover and disclosure history. Reload a view to confirm the information persists.

packs.title: The ten-minute exploration
packs.lead: A suggested route, not an organiser-mandated presentation length.
sections: Sign in to the patient portal. Open Records and Access History. Inspect a document and its recorded access information. Demonstrate a consent change only with the assigned fixture and restoration instructions.
In the staff profile, find the same patient and open the chart. Inspect the reviewed lab document, observations and one stored clinical note. Ask whether the source information survives refresh.
In the pharmacist profile, inspect prescription processing and dispensing history. Distinguish prescribed, dispensed and reconciled medicines.

Inspect a synthetic SBAR handover from the incoming nurse account. Follow the patient association and retained information. Unqualified flowsheet/IV/Morse pathways should not be presented as certified.
Use the assigned simulated tag and authorised responder device. Inspect essential context and the handover patient link. Review the patient-visible emergency disclosure afterwards.
Inspect role navigation and the capability appendix. Ask about adoption and operating cost hypotheses, integration readiness and the next validation milestone.

packs.title: What the demonstration should prove
packs.lead: Evaluate the product through observable transitions.
sections: Can an unfamiliar user find the record, finish a task and understand the next step? Does information read back after refresh and under the correct role?
Does combining patient agency with care-team continuity offer a useful approach? The intended impact is fewer information gaps; measured health outcomes are not claimed.
Is there a credible buyer segment and support/cost model? The facility-subscription model is a positioning hypothesis to investigate.
Does the story demonstrate the app itself? Are alerts and scores explainable from inputs? No autonomous diagnostic or trained predictive-model performance is claimed.

Record the role, build, action and visible error. Distinguish a live product failure from a recorded walkthrough. A video may explain intended behaviour; it cannot replace required usable judge access.
Official judging domains are published in the organiser FAQ [S1]. No numeric weight or pass threshold was found. The ten-minute route is an entrant recommendation.

packs.title: Care that carries forward.
packs.lead: MediChain | Best Health Solution | Proposed three-minute pitch
sections: A patient arrives with a medical story. Every new clinician, shift or emergency responder needs the right part of that story. MediChain gives the patient and the care team connected ways to carry it forward.
Open the patient record, then the staff chart for the same synthetic patient. Show the actual interface immediately. Avoid a long problem-only introduction.
One patient context. Role-specific work. Patient-visible accountability.

packs.title: The patient has a place in the journey
sections: The patient can inspect records and observations, organise appointments and medicines, and communicate with the care team. Consent controls and recorded access history make information use visible.
A stored record, one recorded access reason and the consent interface. Keep synthetic-data identification visible.
This is agency and continuity a person can interact with. Do not claim measured engagement or adherence improvements without data.

packs.title: The care team continues the same story
sections: The clinician sees the chart and reviewed diagnostic evidence. Pharmacy has prescription processing and history. Nursing care and SBAR handover keep the next shift informed. Each role has a task-focused view of the same patient context.
Reviewed lab result in the chart; prescription history; incoming nurse handover. Use currently passing journeys and refresh one view to demonstrate persistence.

MediChain connects the work around the encounter. The broader application also includes specialist, procedure, imaging, preventive and administrative capabilities; the evidence appendix explains their readiness.

packs.title: Urgent context, accountable access
sections: In the responder experience, medical identity and authorised emergency access can surface essential context and carry the patient into ambulance handover. Afterwards, the patient can inspect the recorded disclosure.
Synthetic browser tag scan, scoped demo responder device, patient association and disclosure history. Label the scan as simulated; physical NFC is a separate validation task.
The product pairs useful information with a visible record of its use. Emergency convenience and patient trust belong in the same story.

packs.title: A product with a focused next step
sections: The commercial proposition is a facility offering that connects records, diagnostics-to-treatment and handover. The next positioning decision is how to package these capabilities with transparent onboarding, support and operating cost.
Three connected product tasks: retrieve the record; follow diagnostic evidence into treatment; continue the incoming shift. Use actual app views once hosting is ready.
A coherent facility offering and an operating-cost plan make the application discussable as a sustainable product.

packs.title: Judge the journey. Inspect the evidence.
packs.lead: Closing | 2:35-3:00
sections: MediChain brings patient agency, care-team work and emergency continuity into connected experiences. Explore the patient journey and the transitions between roles. Then inspect the evidence, current limits and the next validation milestone.
App name, Best Health Solution category, verified hosted URL once issued, and the three words: Continuity. Agency. Accountability.

Use the exact submitted release and synthetic fixtures. Add captions; use readable zoom; keep passwords off-screen; ensure audio is clear. Export a small accessible video and test the viewing link privately before submitting.
This is a proposed script and presentation aid. It does not assert that a video or a three-minute pitch is an official submission requirement.

packs.title: Submission requirements and strategy
packs.lead: Internal preparation brief | Public sources checked 7 October 2026
sections: The organiser LinkedIn listing announces entries closing Friday 23 October 2026 and the virtual hackathon running 23-25 October. The closing time and timezone, awards judging days and event date were not found. Submit before the final day and obtain the judging window separately. [S6]

The awards recognise an existing usable app; the hackathon has its own event conditions and themes; the Academy is the learning programme. Do not assume registration or eligibility in one grants entry to the others. [S1, S7, S16]

Enter Best Health Solution first. One category is free; an additional category costs R250 excluding VAT. Enterprise is a possible paid secondary entry only if the professional workflow is strongly qualified. Best Hackathon eligibility needs event-specific confirmation. [S4, S5]
Supporting documents: what is actually known

The live form has a supporting-files upload without a visible mandatory marker or document checklist. No universal requirement for a deck, ID copy, tax certificate, company certificate, video or clinical licence was found. This pack is our recommended persuasive evidence, not an official template. [S2, S3]

Do not submit this access-incomplete draft as a finished entry. Resolve hosted access, current screenshots, factual identity and build proof. Keep all final materials consistent with the live demonstration.

packs.title: Requirements ledger
packs.lead: Required fields, organiser guidance and our recommendations have different status.
sections: Name; company; email; phone; category; app name; publication location; African development location/country; invoice name/address/billing email; terms/privacy acceptance. Billing fields appear even for a free first category. Verify the final live form for conditional changes. [S3]

Telephone; app description; icon; APK/app links; price; supporting files; demo username/password/login process; VAT number; marketing consent. Absence of a visible required marker does not remove the practical need for a useful description and judge access. [S3]
Judges must be able to use a complete solution. Store publication is not essential when remote access and login details are supplied. The FAQ permits screenshot/image upload. [S1]

The supporting-file input allows multiple selection, with no exposed accept filter or required attribute. Maximum size, number, server validation and preferred file formats were not displayed. Do not test by submitting or uploading private documents. [S3]

The publication field provides Other. Use the verified hosted browser URL and describe the patient/staff web experience accurately. Obtain explicit organiser confirmation of PWA/device expectations before relying on that route. [S3]

Review promoter/sponsor affiliation exclusions and accurate-entry obligations. Travel documents concern a travel prize; they are not a universal entry upload. The promoter may request further information. Do not invent documents or entitlement to enter. [S5]

packs.title: How judging should shape the pack
packs.lead: Published domains; no public numeric weighting located.
sections: The FAQ describes two rounds, hands-on app exploration in round one, and three finalists per category. It lists product, creativity, usability, sustainability, impact, presentation and intelligence. [S1]

Working role transitions answer product and usability. Patient-visible access and care continuity support creativity. A buyer proposition and operating model address sustainability. Impact requires measured results when available. A concise connected journey supports presentation. Explainable rules address current intelligence honestly.

The FAQ includes forecasting/pattern-based behaviour, but the current pack does not pretend rule-based scoring is trained predictive AI. Explain current capability and validation; show a future predictive feature only as a future proposal.

The organiser-attributed 2025 release highlights real-world constraints, offline support and accessibility in judge commentary. Treat these as historical qualitative guidance, not 2026 weights. Demonstrate accessible text size now; measure offline/low-data before making claims. [S12]

Vula reports 2025 overall and health wins; health is a serious competitive category. Our response is a clear patient-to-care-team continuity proposition and proof, not unsupported market uniqueness. [S11]
The official roster lists judges but does not label its year. Do not imply personal endorsement or design an entry around guessed individual preferences. No judge was contacted. [S9]

packs.title: A persuasive submission bundle
packs.lead: Recommended packaging, subject to the organiser upload rules.
sections: Seven pages selling the application through patient agency, care-team continuity, trust and a focused adoption hypothesis. Lead upload once factual identity and current proof are confirmed.
Nine pages explaining every capability family, its benefit, source presence, demonstration and current qualification boundary. Use as supporting evidence rather than overwhelming the main story.

Three pages with a suggested ten-minute route. Replace access-status wording with verified URL/account/support instructions before uploading. Put passwords in private form fields, not public marketing PDFs.
Six concise pages for a recorded or live pitch. A three-minute video is recommended, not required by a published rule. Record real current app screens and label synthetic data.
This internal brainstorming brief stays with the team. Its editable inventory, claims ledger and release checklist support later revisions. None of this pack is the final submission.

Capture six current synthetic screenshots and a current screen recording. Use a recognisable icon and consistent name. Keep this workshop edition focused on product structure; external user and pilot material is deferred. Do not attach identity/legal documents merely because the upload is vague.

packs.title: Work backwards from 23 October
packs.lead: Internal targets; organiser closing time still needs confirmation.
sections: Confirm submitter/company, publication status, category and rights to the app. Ask the organiser about PWA eligibility, mandatory files/limits and judging dates. Select the core demonstration and record known limitations.

Create the new AWS account, confirm Free Plan service access, provision the authorised architecture separately, verify HTTPS and backups. Qualify separate-role sessions and all five headline journeys on the actual hosted build.
Capture clean synthetic screenshots and a full successful walkthrough. Record timings only if measured. Resolve or narrow failed paths and make the claims ledger match the build.

Confirm final factual sign-off, add private login details, compress files within confirmed limits, review the mobile experience, test every link from a separate network and submit early. Save entry ID, uploaded versions and any fee receipt.
Keep time for portal failures or organiser clarification. Do not assume midnight or use the hackathon end date as the awards entry deadline.
Keep URLs, credentials, fixture data and funding stable through the organiser-confirmed window. Preserve support availability, backups and the exact submitted release.

packs.title: Questions that public research cannot settle
packs.lead: A ready-to-send organiser enquiry; not sent by this research.
sections: We plan to enter MediChain for Best Health Solution in 2026. It has patient and staff browser/PWA experiences. Please confirm PWA eligibility and device expectations; the 23 October closing time/timezone; awards judging and hosting dates; mandatory supporting documents; maximum file sizes/count and allowed formats; any required pitch/video; and whether demo accounts can be restricted to synthetic data. Please also confirm the final entry portal and how conditional billing fields work for one free category.

The page lists higher education; youth employment/work readiness; youth entrepreneurship/small-business growth; financial inclusion; safer communities/gender-based violence response; and climate resilience/essential services. Healthcare is not listed as a standalone theme. Do not force a fit without organiser guidance. [S7]

Clarify pre-existing code, team rules, theme fit, intellectual property, delivery format and the rubric. The linked registration target returned 404 through the research fetch; this does not prove registration is unavailable in a normal browser. [S7]

LinkedIn public search provided the date announcement; direct access returned a rate-limit response. Social snippets were treated as dated organiser statements, not complete rules. No login, private profile scraping or contact attempt was made.

No complete mandatory-upload checklist, award rubric weights, exact 2026 judging dates, current prize details or complete hackathon rules were verified. Those gaps remain explicit rather than filled with previous-year assumptions.

packs.lead: Public material reviewed; relevant guidance retained and historical rules separated.
sections: Entry page and linked form, FAQ, categories, 2026 terms, contact page, current hackathon themes, organiser LinkedIn and sponsor FNB article. The form was inspected read-only with no personal entry or submission.

Official winner archive; Vula primary winner story and public LinkedIn announcement; organiser-attributed 2025 judge commentary; 2025 programme; a public previous entrant pack; Academy terms. Historical examples inform packaging only.

The FAQ still contains 2025 Academy copy while the form says 2026. The category page and form can differ. LinkedIn gives current October dates while the main terms do not specify a deadline. Recheck final form and organiser messages before submission.
